title: Two lines of cipher signs on the title page of a copy of ad-Dani's at-Taisir, by the scribe Abu Sa'id ibn Humaid (Hamid) ash-Shafi'i al-Muqri' (Berlin, Ms. or. oct. 3629)
correspondents: scribe Abu Sa'id ibn Humaid (Hamid) ash-Shafi'i al-Muqri' (attribution by Sellheim: 'wohl'); no addressee
language: Arabic (presumed from the Arabic manuscript; not established)
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Orientabteilung, Ms. or. oct. 3629 (acc. 1933.30; 'Ahlwardt vor 579'), f. 1a and margin of f. 72b; Sellheim, VOHD XVII A 1 (1976) no. 12
folio_note: f. 1a, between the title and the author's name: 2 lines, '43(?) Buchstaben in Geheimschrift', partly smudged; 7 of them repeated in the margin of f. 72b. Printed facsimile of the two lines: Sellheim, Tafel 55, Abb. 69.
status: Sellheim (1976) p. 23: 'zwischen Titel und Verfasserangabe die beiden Zeilen mit 43(?) Buchstaben in Geheimschrift ... (zum Teil verwischt) und von denen sieben am Rande von Bl. 72b wiederholt sind (s. unten S. 177, sowie Abb. 69 u. 92)'; he gives no reading. Plate caption: '69. Geheimschrift, 615/1217 ? (s. S. 23 u. Abb. 92)'. Seen on the plate at full size: two lines of about 20 separate signs each, several looking like numerals with dots, bare, above the Arabic author line. Sellheim points for comparison to an abjad numeral cipher of c. 1800 in Ms. or. oct. 3938 (Abb. 92), which is written out in clear above its cipher. Not on DECODE.
why: A dated 13th-century Arabic cryptogram by a named Qur'an-reading scholar's scribe, older than nearly every European cipher in the catalogue; probably a name, motto or ownership formula.

date: undated papyrus (Arabic papyri from Egypt are mostly 8th-10th c.; the museum gives no date)
title: Papyrus fragment, one side catalogued 'Arabic', the other 'Cipher (?)' (Penn Museum E16470)
shelfmark: Philadelphia, Penn Museum (University of Pennsylvania Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology), Egyptian Section, E16470 (collector's number Mueller 28a; purchased from Prof. Moritz, 1911)
folio_note: 8.2 x 6.6 cm. Side with the label E 16470: one cursive line and one line of about 9 separate signs (two pairs of strokes, a triangle, a b-like and a box-like sign), then '|| x' below. Other side: 4 lines of thick hooked and looped signs.
status: Museum record: 'Fragment of document. Recto: Arabic. Verso: Cipher (?).' No bibliography, never exhibited. Both images viewed: neither side could be read as Arabic at the size served; the separate signs may be Greek-Coptic numerals or fraction signs (the 'Geheimschrift' of P.Vindob. A. P. 5584 turned out to be dinar-fraction signs, Tyche 34, 2019), and the looped side may be another script. Not established as cipher. Not on DECODE.
why: If the museum's query is right, an early Islamic cipher note on papyrus; more likely numerals, so the first job is identification.
score_note: Scored from the museum record and its two images, viewed during the Arabic sweep part B, 15 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11-15_arabic/); the fragment is only about 520 px across in the images
